description: Single-panel line plot of engineering stress versus engineering strain for Fe-30Mn-9Al-0.8 C low-density steel after different multiaxial forging (MAF) passes. The x-axis is "Engineering strain" spanning 0.0-0.8 (major ticks every 0.1); the y-axis is "Engineering stress (MPa)" spanning 0-1600 (major ticks every 200). An upper-right legend identifies four curves: MAF-0 (grey), MAF-1 (red), MAF-3 (blue), MAF-5 (green). The grey MAF-0 curve starts near the 400 MPa gridline, work-hardens continuously to a broad maximum between the 600 and 800 MPa gridlines at strain ≈0.6-0.7, then softens to roughly 550 MPa, ending near strain 0.75 — the most ductile condition. The three forged conditions are much stronger but fail early. MAF-5 (green) begins highest, near the 1600 MPa level at zero strain, and falls steeply, crossing the other curves and ending near 1250 MPa by strain ≈0.15. MAF-3 (blue) peaks near 1400 MPa at small strain and drops to about 1240 MPa at strain ≈0.13. MAF-1 (red) starts between 1000 and 1200 MPa, rises to a maximum between 1200 and 1400 MPa at strain ≈0.25, and fractures near strain 0.3. The figure thus demonstrates a strength-ductility trade-off with increasing MAF passes. No numeric data labels are printed on the curves.

observations.observation: The plot axes are Engineering strain (0.0-0.8, ticks every 0.1) on x and Engineering stress (MPa) (0-1600, ticks every 200) on y.
Four curves are distinguished by an upper-right legend: MAF-0 (grey), MAF-1 (red), MAF-3 (blue) and MAF-5 (green).

The grey MAF-0 curve is the only one that reaches large strain: it starts at about the 400 MPa level, rises gradually to a broad maximum between the 600 and 800 MPa gridlines near strain 0.6-0.7, then drops to roughly 550 MPa around strain 0.75.
The green MAF-5 curve begins at the highest stress of all four curves, just below the 1600 MPa gridline at near-zero strain, and decreases steeply to about 1250 MPa by strain ~0.15, where it stops.
The blue MAF-3 curve shows a peak between the 1200 and 1400 MPa gridlines at very low strain and then decreases, ending near 1240 MPa at strain ~0.13.
The red MAF-1 curve starts between the 1000 and 1200 MPa gridlines, rises to its maximum (between 1200 and 1400 MPa) at strain ~0.25, and falls to ~1180 MPa at strain ~0.3 where it terminates.
All three forged curves (MAF-1, MAF-3, MAF-5) terminate before strain 0.35, whereas MAF-0 continues past strain 0.7, showing the strength-ductility trade-off produced by MAF.
No numeric stress or strain values are printed on the curves themselves; all curve positions must be read against the axis gridlines.
The caption states the figure shows engineering stress-strain plots after different MAF passes.
The citing text states the solutionized and quenched coarse-grained MAF-0 steel displays the lowest yield strength, 380 MPa.
The citing text states that after 1 MAF pass the yield strength increases drastically, by about three times, to 1040 MPa.
The citing text attributes the strengthening after 1 pass mainly to a dislocation density increase to 5.57 x 10^15 m^-2 and a marginal grain-size refinement from 50 µm to 35 µm.
The citing text states that further MAF to 3 passes raises the yield strength further (sentence truncated), consistent with the higher curves for MAF-3 and MAF-5 in the plot.

subfigures.description: Engineering stress-strain curves (stress 0-1600 MPa vs strain 0.0-0.8) for four conditions labelled in the legend: MAF-0 (grey), MAF-1 (red), MAF-3 (blue), MAF-5 (green). The grey MAF-0 curve is lowest in stress (starting near 400 MPa) but extends to the largest strain (~0.75); the red, blue and green curves are all above ~1000 MPa but terminate before strain 0.35.
